A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SelfReflect research. All pages, including appendices, were readable, and the text, equations, figures, and tables could be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V3 reports original summary-discrimination experiments, MMLU comparisons, a human study, model-generation benchmarks, and finetuning results, including Tables 1–5 and 16.

after.justification: V4 retains those empirical studies and adds InfoSumm comparisons, sampling analyses, HotpotQA evaluation, and self-critique results.

M1.justification: The SelfReflect metric and existing training procedures are unchanged. Appendix O adds a generation variant that critiques and revises a Sample & Summarize response using ten further answer samples after the initial ten-sample summary. This adds a limited inference step.

E1.justification: Appendix M adds HotpotQA evaluation with supplied Wikipedia background for nine existing models, extending the closed-book experiments to a context-provided QA scenario. Natural Questions, TriviaQA, SimpleQA, and MMLU coverage is retained.

E2.justification: V4 adds InfoSumm to the summary-discrimination comparison in Table 1 and compares Self-Critique against Sample & Summarize in Table 20. Existing comparators are retained; InfoSumm is not added to the MMLU or human-preference comparisons in Tables 2–3.

E3.justification: The main evaluation settings remain unchanged. Added protocols vary masked-answer count M from 1 to 50 while fixing reference count N=50, extend summary-generation sample counts to 100, and provide ten additional samples for self-critique. Stopword exclusion mentioned in v4 Section 3.2 was already documented in v3 Appendix F.1.

E4.justification: V4 substantially expands diagnostics beyond v3's joint N=M convergence analysis and CoT confusion matrices. It adds an M-only sensitivity study, examples covering all four CoT certainty quadrants, a summary-length and sample-count analysis, and tests of whether self-critique improves summaries (Appendices B.2, K.2, N, and O).

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals and use 100 bootstrap samples for the human-study intervals. New InfoSumm and sampling-analysis rows follow the existing reporting practice; no changed seed, repeated-run, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and finetuning entries are retained, but substantial results are added. InfoSumm achieves 99.87% good-versus-bad discrimination versus SelfReflect's 98.77%, but 60.81% versus 93.20% on good-versus-almost-good summaries (Table 1). Tables 6 and 18–20 add sampling, HotpotQA, length, and mixed self-critique outcomes. Self-critique receives extra samples, so these are not equal-budget performance gains.

T1.justification: SelfReflect's definitions, assumptions, propositions, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged. Appendix E.9 adds a limited mathematical construction of the InfoSumm comparator, including per-answer saliency averaging and combining saliency with faithfulness in Equations E.1–E.4.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central contributions: a predictive-sufficiency-based faithfulness metric and evidence that direct prompting, reasoning, and finetuning fail to reliably summarize internal answer distributions, whereas sampling and feeding answers back supports faithful summaries. Additional experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V4 attributes smaller RAG advantages to more concentrated answer distributions and discusses excessive listing, score saturation, and alternative descriptions of high-variance uncertainty. The fixed-N analysis also adds an interpretation of convergence failure. The limitations in Section 7 already appeared in v3 Appendix B.

D1.justification: Appendix E.9 documents the InfoSumm implementation, Section 4.3 adds a Krippendorff-alpha software link, and Appendix O specifies the extra samples used for critique. A reproducibility statement is added, while the main repository URL, hardware information, existing prompts, and finetuning hyperparameters were already supplied in v3.

R1.justification: V4 adds Jung et al. (2024) for InfoSumm and Yang et al. (2018) for HotpotQA. It explicitly relates SelfReflect to InfoSumm's masked-task information estimation, while retaining the broader positioning within uncertainty quantification and summarization.

P1.justification: V4 rewrites the baseline and MMLU explanations, adds an anthropomorphic-language clarification and reproducibility statement, and moves existing limitations into Section 7. Appendices are extended and renumbered, but most prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains an InfoSumm row and updated best-result emphasis; Tables 6 and 18–20 are added. Existing displays are relocated or reflowed, including convergence plots and the licensing table. The figures' substantive content and overall visual design are retained.

improvement.justification: The added InfoSumm comparison, contextual QA evaluation, and sampling, length, and self-critique analyses strengthen validation and clarify practical behavior beyond v3's already substantial evidence. These are useful incremental gains. Their value is tempered by reporting inconsistencies: Table 6 is labeled Natural Questions, but several baseline rows match pooled Table 1 values rather than the Natural Questions entries in Table 10.
